summary: Separates database migration configuration from application authentication and encryption secrets for least-privilege deployment jobs.
userImpact: Database migration and readiness jobs can start with only their database-scoped configuration and credentials.

instructions: Redeploy the matching host chart and backend image so database jobs use the database-only configuration boundary.

configuration: No new environment variables are required; existing database, tenancy, schema-epoch, and adapter settings retain their names and defaults.
Migration and preflight jobs must continue to mount their dedicated database Secrets and must not receive JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, or ENCRYPTION_KEY.

notes: No schema migration is added and the PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, and Spanner TypeORM adapter contracts are unchanged.
Pooled-tenancy, owner migration, schema-epoch preflight, RLS, and runtime-grant behavior remain enabled through database-scoped configuration.

security: Application authentication, administrator, and encryption secrets are no longer prerequisites of the migration module graph or inputs to database migration and preflight jobs.
The application runtime retains full production validation of JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and ENCRYPTION_KEY.
documentation: The host chart operator documentation describes the database-only configuration boundary for migration and preflight jobs.
knownLimitations: Database credentials remain adapter-specific and must still be scoped separately for owner migration, preflight, and application runtime identities.
rollback: Redeploy the prior matching backend image and host chart; no database rollback or data restoration is required.
validation: Focused configuration and module-boundary tests prove production migration imports succeed without application secrets.
Negative configuration tests prove every supported adapter still rejects missing required connection fields and PostgreSQL still rejects the public application schema.
TypeORM adapter, migration orchestration, Helm rendering, PostgreSQL integration, and database portability gates cover the unchanged database behavior.
